title: Cohomological boundedness of stratified dualizable condensed sheaves
statement: Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $B=p_Y^*\Lambda$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(B)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with ordinary relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $K\in D(B)$ admit a finite stratification of $Y$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset], on each of which its derived restriction is dualizable: there are an object $D$ and evaluation $D\otimes K\to B$ and coevaluation $B\to K\otimes D$ with the two contraction composites equal to the identities, using the usual associators and unitors [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Then there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $H^j(K)=0$ for $j<a$ and for $j>b$. In particular, $K$ has a cochain representative $C^\bullet$ with $C^j=0$ for every $j<a$. No Noetherian, finite-dimensional, or regularity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: Each constructible stratum is retrocompact by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-is-retrocompact], hence quasi-compact since Y is quasi-compact. The stratum immersion is a topological embedding and identifies its domain with the stratum. Thus each domain is quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], its immersion into the quasi-separated Y is quasi-compact.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: For any quasi-compact scheme T and dualizable L, apply [det-pe-hypercover-single-cover] to the terminal object to obtain a singleton covering Spec D → T with D w-contractible. Transport w-contractibility through the canonical ring isomorphism D ≅ Γ(Spec D,O); the private helper proves ring-equivalence invariance directly from the w-local, strictly henselian localization and extremally disconnected component definitions. Pullback preserves L's exact pairing by [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality]. On Spec D the equivalence of [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] realizes the pulled-back L as F(P) for a perfect complex P over the actual section ring.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: By [lem-sf-perfect-ring-classical-generator], perfect complexes form the thick subcategory generated by A[0]. The inverse image of bounded objects under the exact realization F is triangulated (Mathlib t-structure bounded-subcategory and inverse-image instances), and is closed under retracts: homology sends a retract to a retract, so vanishing outside an interval descends to the retract. This inverse image contains A[0] because F is strong monoidal and its target unit is the coefficient sheaf in degree zero. The triangEnvelope universal property therefore proves F(P) bounded, and the evaluation isomorphism proves the pulled-back L bounded.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: Exact termwise inverse image commutes with homology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. For q outside the bounds on the singleton cover, the restriction of H^q(L) is zero. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative] to H^q(L)[0], using the exact-functor single-complex comparison; its degree-zero homology is H^q(L), so this sheaf is zero. Thus L is bounded on T.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: Apply the preceding argument to each given dualizable stratum restriction. Choose lower and upper integer bounds a_i,b_i, and set a=-Σ_i|a_i|, b=Σ_i|b_i|. Then a≤a_i and b_i≤b for every i, and a≤0≤b, including an empty index family. For q<a or b<q, every restricted homology sheaf vanishes. The coefficient comparison identifies the underlying sheaf of module inverse image with abelian inverse image. The stratum immersions are a finite quasi-compact jointly surjective family by step 1 and the stratification range/union equations. Apply [lem-pod-finite-qc-proetale-abelian-detection] to the identity of the underlying abelian sheaf of H^q(K). Faithfulness of module forgetting makes H^q(K) zero.

source.place: Corollary 4.11 and Lemma 4.10, with constructibility as in Definition 3.3

proof.text: The lower homology bound gives K.IsGE a. Apply the existing Mathlib theorem DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE to obtain a cochain representative C with Q(C) ≅ K and C strictly zero below a. This is the good lower truncation of [def-kun-truncations]; no new representative construction is needed.
